module-0-student-roster-project.label: Module 0 First-Week Roster Check
module-0-student-roster-project.summary: Verify that the school roster workspace responds and that the imported student table can be inspected before staff rely on it.

mp-1-preview-student-roster.title: Confirm the SQL workspace responds
mp-1-preview-student-roster.prompt: The roster check is starting. Return `'Roster check started' AS status` as a one-row result. Run it and confirm the `status` column appears.
mp-1-preview-student-roster.hint: Use the one-row SELECT pattern from the environment lesson, with the new value requested here.

help.concept: Before checking imported data, verify that the SQL workspace can execute a query and return a readable result.
help.hint_1: This step does not use a table.
help.hint_2: Return the text `Roster check started` with the column name `status`.

mp-1-preview-student-roster.starterCode:
-- Confirm that the SQL workspace is responding.
SELECT

mp-2-add-city-to-roster.title: Inspect the imported roster
mp-2-add-city-to-roster.prompt: The workspace is responding. Now inspect the imported roster by returning every available column from the `students` table.
mp-2-add-city-to-roster.hint: Use the all-columns form shown as a preview earlier in the module.

help.concept: This step checks that the imported `students` table is visible and readable before staff rely on it.
help.hint_1: You need the full table, not a hand-picked column list.
help.hint_2: Use `*` to inspect every available column from `students`.

module-0-student-roster-project.label: Module 0 Student Roster Project
module-0-student-roster-project.summary: Build a simple student roster that becomes more useful with each step.

mp-1-preview-student-roster.title: Preview the roster columns
mp-1-preview-student-roster.prompt: Start the student roster by returning `id`, `name`, and `grade` from the `students` table.
mp-1-preview-student-roster.hint: Add the missing field in the SELECT list.

help.concept: This step adds one more detail to the roster so it is easier to use.
help.hint_1: Keep `id` and `name`, then add `grade` before `FROM students`.
help.hint_2: Run the query and check that the result shows three columns in that order.

mp-1-preview-student-roster.starterCode:
-- Returning id, name, and grade from the students table.
SELECT
  id,
  name
FROM students;

mp-2-add-city-to-roster.title: Add each student's city
mp-2-add-city-to-roster.prompt: Add the `city` column so the roster shows where each student is from.
mp-2-add-city-to-roster.hint: Extend the SELECT list instead of starting over.

help.concept: Add the new detail without changing the parts of the roster that already work.
help.hint_1: Keep `id`, `name`, and `grade` exactly as they are.
help.hint_2: Add `city` before `FROM students`, then rerun the query.

mp-2-add-city-to-roster.starterCode:
-- Keep the roster fields above.
-- Add city before FROM students.
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  grade
FROM students;

mp-3-finish-student-roster.title: Finish the full roster view
mp-3-finish-student-roster.prompt: Add `age` so the final roster returns `id`, `name`, `grade`, `age`, and `city` from `students`.
mp-3-finish-student-roster.hint: Insert one more field into the SELECT list.

help.concept: This last step completes the roster with the final missing field.
help.hint_2: Add `age` between `grade` and `city`, then rerun the query.

mp-3-finish-student-roster.starterCode:
-- Keep the roster fields above.
-- Add age between grade and city.
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  grade,
  city
FROM students;

sketch_project_brief.title: The roster import needs a quick verification.
sketch_project_brief.bodyMarkdown:
It is Monday morning before the first week of classes. The school office has imported its student roster, but nobody wants to hand it to staff until someone confirms that the SQL workspace is responding and the roster table is actually readable.

You are doing that first verification.

You will not build a report yet. That comes in the next module, after you learn how to choose specific columns deliberately.

For this project you will:

1. run a small status query to prove the SQL workspace responds;
2. inspect the complete `students` table so you can confirm the imported roster is visible.

The goal is a trustworthy first check, not a long query.

sketch_project_brief.title: Project brief
sketch_project_brief.bodyMarkdown:
The school office is preparing a roster snapshot for the first week of classes.

Start with a simple student list, then add the details that make the roster useful at a glance.

The finished result should present each student's key information in one clean view.
